clinicalQuestion: Can completion axillary lymph-node dissection be omitted in selected patients with 1–2 positive sentinel nodes undergoing breast-conserving therapy?
population: Women with cT1–2, clinically node-negative invasive breast cancer and 1–2 sentinel-node metastases undergoing lumpectomy, whole-breast irradiation and systemic therapy
absoluteEffect: OS 86.3% vs 83.6%: +2.7 percentage points, meeting non-inferiority; DFS 80.2% vs 78.2%.
toxicityQoL: Omission avoids the morbidity of ALND; nodal recurrence remained rare in both groups.
interpretation: For appropriately selected cT1–2 patients with 1–2 positive sentinel nodes treated with breast-conserving therapy, routine completion ALND does not improve survival.

clinicalQuestion: Can completion axillary dissection be omitted when 1–2 sentinel nodes contain macrometastases?
population: Clinically node-negative breast cancer with 1–2 sentinel-node macrometastases, including selected mastectomy patients
toxicityQoL: Axillary recurrence was very uncommon; avoiding ALND reduces surgical morbidity.
interpretation: SENOMAC broadens axillary de-escalation beyond the classic Z0011 population, although radiation and systemic therapy remain integral to the treatment context.

clinicalQuestion: If axillary treatment is required after a positive sentinel node, can axillary radiotherapy replace ALND?
population: cT1–2, clinically node-negative breast cancer with a positive sentinel node
absoluteEffect: 10-year axillary recurrence 1.82% with axillary RT vs 0.93% with ALND: +0.89 percentage point; no OS or DFS difference.
toxicityQoL: 5-year lymphedema was 11.9% with axillary RT vs 24.5% with ALND; QoL scales did not differ significantly.
interpretation: Axillary RT provides excellent regional control comparable to ALND while substantially reducing lymphedema and is a strong de-escalation option when axillary treatment is indicated.

clinicalQuestion: Can regional nodal irradiation be omitted after neoadjuvant therapy converts biopsy-proven node-positive disease to ypN0?
population: Patients initially cN1 who became ypN0 after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, undergoing breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy
absoluteEffect: 5-year freedom from invasive breast-cancer recurrence or death 92.7% vs 91.8%: +0.9 percentage point, not statistically significant.
toxicityQoL: Grade 4 adverse events were uncommon: 0.5% with RNI vs 0.1% without.
interpretation: For appropriately selected patients with initial cN1 disease who become ypN0 after neoadjuvant therapy, routine RNI did not improve invasive recurrence-free outcomes.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab and chemotherapy improve outcomes in HER2-positive early breast cancer?
population: HER2-positive early breast cancer receiving adjuvant chemotherapy and trastuzumab
absoluteEffect: 8-year iDFS 88.4% vs 85.8%: absolute benefit 2.6 percentage points; node-positive benefit was larger at 4.9 points.
toxicityQoL: Diarrhea and other treatment-related toxicity are increased with pertuzumab; the absolute efficacy benefit is concentrated in node-positive disease.
interpretation: The incremental benefit of adjuvant pertuzumab is modest overall but clinically more relevant in node-positive HER2-positive disease.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding abemaciclib to endocrine therapy reduce recurrence in high-risk HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer?
population: High-risk node-positive HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer
absoluteEffect: 5-year iDFS approximately 83.6% vs 76.0%: absolute benefit about 7.6 percentage points.
toxicityQoL: Diarrhea, neutropenia and treatment discontinuation are important trade-offs with abemaciclib.
interpretation: Adjuvant abemaciclib produces a clinically meaningful reduction in recurrence for selected high-risk node-positive HR-positive/HER2-negative disease.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding 3 years of ribociclib to an aromatase inhibitor improve invasive disease-free survival across stage II–III HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer?
population: Stage II–III HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer
absoluteEffect: 4-year iDFS 88.5% vs 83.6%: absolute benefit 4.9 percentage points.
toxicityQoL: Neutropenia and other CDK4/6 inhibitor toxicities require monitoring; overall survival data remain immature.
interpretation: Three years of adjuvant ribociclib adds a sustained recurrence reduction across the broad NATALEE population, with survival benefit not yet mature.

clinicalQuestion: Does one year of adjuvant olaparib improve outcomes in germline BRCA1/2-mutated, high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer?
population: High-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer with a germline pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant after local therapy and chemotherapy
absoluteEffect: 4-year IDFS 82.7% vs 75.4%: absolute benefit 7.3 percentage points; DDFS benefit 7.4 points; OS difference 3.4 points.
toxicityQoL: Anemia, nausea and fatigue are important treatment toxicities; treatment is limited to one year.
interpretation: For germline BRCA1/2-mutated high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer, adjuvant olaparib provides a substantial reduction in recurrence and distant recurrence with an emerging survival benefit.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding pembrolizumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab improve survival in early triple-negative breast cancer?
population: Early-stage triple-negative breast cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy
intervention: Pembrolizumab + neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab
comparator: Placebo + neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by placebo
absoluteEffect: 5-year OS 86.6% vs 81.7%: absolute survival benefit 4.9 percentage points.
toxicityQoL: Immune-related adverse events add to chemotherapy toxicity and can be persistent or require corticosteroid treatment.
interpretation: Perioperative pembrolizumab improves both event-free outcomes and overall survival in appropriately selected early triple-negative breast cancer.

clinicalQuestion: Does one year of adjuvant trastuzumab improve long-term survival in HER2-positive early breast cancer?
population: HER2-positive early breast cancer after surgery and chemotherapy
relativeEffect: Approximately HR 0.76 for DFS in long-term analyses
absoluteEffect: Trastuzumab produces a durable reduction in recurrence and a clinically meaningful long-term survival benefit compared with observation.
nnt: Depends on baseline risk and time horizon
toxicityQoL: Cardiac dysfunction is the major clinically important toxicity and requires cardiac monitoring.
interpretation: A year of adjuvant trastuzumab established anti-HER2 therapy as a major component of curative treatment for HER2-positive early breast cancer.
